newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No end in sight to Belgian share strength.
newsitem.headline: No end in sight to Belgian share strength.

text.p: Belgian shares, which ended a see-saw Friday with bond and U.S. consumer price-fuelled gains, look set to continue climbing as positive sentiment runs rampant over caution, traders said.
"We believe the market is too high. But there is no overall downside pressure," one trader said.
The Bel-20 index finished 4.63 points or 0.26 percent higher at 1,757.92 after trading in a 1,762.84/1,747.69 range and with the all-time high of 1,781 now within sight.
There were 12 gainers, two unchanged and six losers. Total market volume was two billion francs.
Kredietbank, which on Thursday after the close of play reported half year profits up 14.5 percent, was the star of the day, up three percent to 10,300 francs.
Traders said it was also helped by the prospect of its reweighting next Friday in the Bel-20.

Electronic stock Barco, which on Thursday plunged 7.4 percent after management warned of slower profit growth, staged a mild recovery, gaining 0.6 percent to 5,040 francs. Barco has been the market's darling for some time.
"Just because the management choses to be cautious does not mean you have to punish the stock," one trader said.
Traders said that while the bull sentiment of the Belgian market showed no sign of flagging, players would still take note of how the Dow Jones performed and U.S. data next week.
August industrial production figures are due on Tuesday, followed by housing starts on Thursday.
